I miss my wife something fierce, and it’s hard to find a reason to do much. I don’t cook, don’t clean—my son says the house is a mess. I told him once I’d take my old truck down to the reservoir, maybe in the morning when it’s quiet, and not come back. I didn’t truly want to, but I thought through how I might… just to stop the weight.

But then, for about a month last winter, it was like that sadness lifted. Not happy, exactly—more restless. I’d sleep two or three hours and be up pacing, fixing things around the house I didn’t need to fix. I talked at my neighbor for near an hour about nothing at all—furnace filters, my late wife’s hydrangeas—I couldn’t seem to stop. I felt wound up, like my skin was too tight.

Lately, I’ve swung back again—tired, slow, not caring. I worry some—about money, about my health—but I can’t tell if that’s just getting older or something more. The thoughts race, but I don’t know why.

But before this, there was this weird month where everything flipped. I wasn’t tired at all—I’d sleep maybe four hours and wake up feeling wired. I couldn’t sit still, paced around the house, tapped my fingers, shuffled papers without purpose. I snapped at my grandson over nothing. Talked so much my daughter said I didn’t let anyone get a word in. I didn’t *feel* anxious—just restless, on edge in a different way. My mind raced, but it wasn’t about worry; it was like ideas just kept coming, one after another, making me jump from one thing to the next.  

The anxious feelings come and go, but those racing thoughts and the urge to move—they don’t stem from anxiety. They just come with their own energy.

D009-D011_h025.question_both:
I’ve been feeling off for over a year now—like I’m dragging myself through everything. Even after a full night’s sleep, my body feels heavy, like just walking to the bike shop or carrying a delivery wears me out. I used to care about my ratings as a courier, hitting targets, saving up—but now it just doesn’t seem to matter much. I’ll get on my bike, but half the time I end up pacing outside the pickup spot, going over the same thoughts, or picking at my fingers without realizing it.  

Then there are stretches—lately, about the past three months—where it’s like my engine’s stuck in high gear. I’ll take ten deliveries in a row, even do side gigs late into the night. Sleep? I’ll crash when I pass out, but not because I feel tired. But if someone slows me down or gives me trouble, I snap—little things set me off.  

It’s not constant. I don’t know if this is anxiety, stress, or just burnout. The worry’s there sometimes, but honestly, I can’t tell if it’s driving the thoughts—or if the thoughts even need a reason. Nothing feels extreme, just... stuck in a loop.
D009-D011_h025.question_a:
I’ve been feeling pretty down for over a year now—just constantly tired, like my body’s made of concrete. Even small rides for work leave me drained. I can’t seem to care about stuff I used to, like finishing shifts early or getting good ratings. I pace a lot when I’m waiting for orders, just walking in circles, wringing my hands—my mind’s restless, but I’m not doing anything with it.

Before this low hit, though, there was this 3-month stretch last year where I was the opposite. I was angry all the time—road rage, snapping at people over tiny things. But I didn’t sleep, not really. I’d ride all night, take double shifts, start side gigs—didn’t feel tired at all. I didn’t care if I slept; I just kept moving.

Now, I do get anxious—racing thoughts, jittery—especially about money or being late. But when I had those bursts of energy or made impulsive decisions, like spending all my cash on gear I didn’t need, it wasn’t because I was worried. I wasn’t overthinking—I just *did* it. The anxiety’s there, but the impulsivity and speed of my thoughts feel separate, like they have their own rhythm.
D009-D011_h025.question_b:
I’ve been feeling down for over a year now—just constantly drained, like my body’s made of lead. Even small rides tire me out, and I can’t seem to care about anything, not even when I finish a bunch of deliveries fast. I used to push hard, though—last winter I was riding way more than usual, taking every shift, felt like I didn’t need sleep. I’d stay up all night, irritated if anyone slowed me down, snapping at customers over tiny things. But I wasn’t *happy*—just wired, restless.  

Lately, it’s like my mind won’t shut up. I worry nonstop—about money, accidents, deadlines, dumb things—racing thoughts that spiral out of control. When I get anxious, I start pacing, can’t sit on my bike between orders, and my hands won’t stop fidgeting. The weird thing is, those fast thoughts and the urge to move—they don’t come out of nowhere. They *follow* the worry. It’s not like I’m impulsively chasing ideas—I’m stuck ruminating, and *that’s* what makes me feel jittery and overactive. That restless phase a while back? I think it was just anxiety in overdrive, not some separate high.
